title: Hyundai and LGES launch battery storage pilot using repurposed EV batteries - electrive.com
content:
Hyundai and Kia are collaborating with LG Energy Solution on a large-scale demonstration project for charging stations with battery storage systems as an external buffer, using second-life batteries from EVs on the E-GMP platform.
Image: Hyundai
The goal of the pilot project in South Korea is to determine whether batteries decommissioned from EVs can find a profitable second life as energy storage systems for charging electric vehicles – i.e. second-life applications. The project utilises battery packs from EVs based on Hyundai Motor Group’s E-GMP platform. According to the companies, this marks the first such demonstration in South Korea to employ decommissioned E-GMP battery packs.
The system, installed at Wonik PNE’s plant in Dongtan, Hwaseong, south of Seoul, has a storage capacity of 200 kWh. The UBESS (Ultra-Burned Energy Storage System) is connected to DC fast chargers for EVs. The installation primarily stores energy in the UBESS during off-peak hours, when electricity prices are low, and then uses the fast chargers to charge electric vehicles during peak demand periods.
Hyundai and Kia aim to develop a business model
As part of the UBESS project, sister brands Hyundai and Kia are working to develop a business model for establishing a system that enables the safe and efficient use of repurposed batteries. LG Energy Solution manufactures UBESS systems using used battery packs from Hyundai Motor and Kia, and supports the verification of system performance and safety through its battery diagnostics and operational technology.
Drawing on its experience in operating EV charging infrastructure, Hyundai Engineering is evaluating business development in real-world commercial environments and the integration with the business of building EV charging infrastructure. Meanwhile, Wonik PNE, a manufacturer of charging stations, is responsible for stable system operation and technical verification based on its expertise in charger manufacturing and infrastructure construction.
Leveraging their respective expertise, the participating companies plan to comprehensively evaluate charging/discharging control algorithms, system safety and reliability, battery performance retention characteristics, charging quality, and operational efficiency. They will also test the feasibility of reusing repurposed batteries and the implementation of a circular battery economy in real-world commercial environments, according to Hyundai.
The use of repurposed EV batteries in stationary energy storage systems is not new. For example, Porsche established a stationary energy storage system two years ago to power its Leipzig plant, utilising used batteries from the Taycan. Additionally, there are already DC fast chargers with integrated battery storage, such as those from
ELMI Power
. However, what sets Hyundai and its partners’ project apart is the combination of repurposed batteries in a stationary storage system connected to a DC fast charger.

title: General Motors introduces recycled battery materials in customer vehicles - electrive.com
content:
General Motors has built its first production vehicles with battery cells whose cathode active material is made entirely from recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese. The raw materials are partly sourced from decommissioned batteries of GM vehicles and were recovered and processed by partner Cirba Solutions.
Assembly of battery with recycled cathode material
Image: General Motors
General Motors, together with recycling company
Cirba Solutions
and other partners, has completed a pilot project for a closed-loop recycling system for electric vehicle batteries. In this initiative, end-of-life batteries from GM EVs – including from brands like Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC – were recycled, with the recovered raw materials reused to produce new battery cells. The standout feature: the cathode active material (CAM) of the new cells is made entirely from recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese. The first EVs equipped with these cells have already left GM’s factories – not as internal test vehicles for validation, but as regular production EVs for customers.
For the pilot project, General Motors collected 80 end-of-life high-voltage batteries, which were processed by Cirba Solutions at a recycling facility in Ohio, USA. After mechanical processing, the initial output was a so-called black mass, which was further refined to separate the contained raw materials. This process yielded more than 12 tonnes of new cathode active material. The nickel, cobalt, and manganese in this material were 100 per cent recycled. Before being used in new battery cells, the material had to meet the same quality, performance, and safety requirements as material sourced from primary raw materials.
GM deploying recycled materials in series production
The production of the new cells was handled by Ultium Cells, the battery joint venture between GM and LG Energy Solution. The cells were then assembled into battery modules and packs at GM’s Factory ZERO and Spring Hill plants. According to General Motors, the first vehicles to feature these recycled-material cells include the Cadillac Lyriq, Lyriq-V, Vistiq, Escalade IQ, and Escalade IQL, as well as the Chevrolet Silverado EV Trail Boss and the GMC Sierra EV AT4. GM emphasises that the cells demonstrated performance comparable to those made from new raw materials during testing.
GMC Sierra EV with a battery made from recycled cathode material
GM views the pilot project as a test for a future growing source of raw materials. According to the company, current recycling processes can recover up to 95 per cent of the nickel, cobalt, and manganese, and up to 80 per cent of the lithium, depending on the process and cell chemistry. As the number of end-of-life electric vehicle batteries increases, so too will the volume of secondary raw materials. GM is pursuing a multi-stage approach: batteries should first be used in vehicles for as long as possible, then refurbished or repurposed for stationary storage applications, and only recycled at the end of their lifecycle. For example, GM plans to work with Redwood Materials to repurpose around 10,000 batteries from electric vehicles for stationary applications.
The closed-loop system is not only significant from a sustainability perspective. Nickel, cobalt, and other battery raw materials are key cost and risk factors in cell production. Recovering and reintegrating them into cell manufacturing after the end of a battery’s life can reduce long-term demand for newly mined raw materials and improve supply security. For General Motors, as a US manufacturer, regional value creation is also critical: the batteries are processed in North America, and the recovered materials are fed back into local cell and vehicle production.
Porsche pursues similar approach
Just last week, Porsche, together with the Aachen-based recycling company Cylib,
unveiled
a very similar pilot project. There, too, battery cells were produced for the first time with cathode active material made entirely from recycled raw materials. Unlike GM’s approach, Porsche’s includes lithium in addition to nickel, cobalt, and manganese; the raw materials are sourced from end-of-life high-voltage batteries from Porsche’s own vehicles. However, Porsche is still testing the cells produced from these materials in prototype vehicles, and integration into customer vehicles has not yet taken place.
The key difference lies in the maturity of the two projects: Porsche is still in the testing phase with its recycling cells, aiming to use the findings as a basis for potential future use in series production batteries. At GM, on the other hand, the recycling cells have already been incorporated into battery packs of electric vehicles that have left the factory and been delivered to customers. Porsche also intends to close the loop all the way to series production in the future: since May 2026, old batteries from German Porsche centres have been recycled together with Cylib, and the recovered raw materials are expected to be available for new battery cells from 2028.

title: Australia’s Sicona acquires Advano to expand silicon-carbon battery tech in US – Batteries International
content: Australia-headquartered Sicona Battery Technologies has acquired 100% of New Orleans battery tech company Advano, giving it a US operating based including a pilot manufacturing plant, R&D labs and cell-testing equipment. Sicona confirmed the deal, for an undisclosed sum, on September 16. The announcement came just weeks after Sicona secured a funding boost of up to A$45 million ($31 million) to demonstrate manufacturing of its advanced silicon-carbon battery anode material in Australia. The company plans to install its own SiCx silicon-carbon anode production process at the US plant to support Advano’s existing US customers — and expand the New Orleans operation into what it called a ‘super pilot’ facility to produce enough material for over three million battery cells. The facility will target a wide variety of applications including AI datacentre battery backup systems, robotics, power tools, autonomous systems, drones, electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft and defence. Sicona said the acquisition will solidify its position as one of the leading IP holders in the field of mechanical silicon anode materials and consolidate Advano’s silicon anode patent portfolio. Advano, founded in 2016, has developed a silicon-based anode material designed to increase lithium ion battery energy density and reduce cost per kilowatt hour. The company has raised around $46 million to date. Sicona founder and CEO Christiaan Jordaan said the deal has particular significance, coming as two US laws shift the economics of battery production towards American plants. From October 2027, one law prevents procurement of batteries produced by certain Chinese battery manufacturers while another already pays companies 10% of battery anode material production costs, if made within the US. Jordaan said Sicona will produce anode material inside the US before the 2027 restrictions take effect, which will allow an Australian company to compete for American contracts on price and origin. According to Sicona, its US plans have also been conditionally selected for unspecified congressional appropriations funding. Meanwhile, distinguished energy storage scientist Shirley Meng, most recently chief scientist at the Argonne Collaborative Center for Energy Storage Science, will join Sicona as scientific adviser. Meng said silicon-based anodes have the potential to deliver major improvements in battery energy, power and charging performance, but successful commercialisation depends on materials that can be manufactured safely, economically and at meaningful scale. title: Battery Fire Evacuates 500—New Tech Could Stop the Next One
content:
Stationary Batteries
Testing & Safety
Thermal Management
Battery News
As California firefighters battle thermal runaway across multiple storage systems, researchers are developing VOC monitoring, acoustic detection, and immersion cooling to prevent cascade failures.
September 23, 2026
At a Glance
Thermal runaway spread to second battery system at California water facility, keeping 500 homes evacuated since Tuesday.
Acoustic AI and VOC monitoring systems can detect battery failures minutes before thermal runaway begins, researchers say.
09/24/2026 Update
: According to local reporting, the number of homes under evacuation orders because of the battery fire
is now 500
rather than the 200 we originally reported.
A lithium-ion battery fire at a Metropolitan Water District facility in La Verne, California, has kept approximately 200 homes under evacuation orders since Tuesday, underscoring the persistent safety challenges facing battery energy storage systems (BESS) as they become increasingly critical to grid infrastructure.
The incident
The fire began at 11:40 a.m. on Tuesday, September 22, following a "minor explosion" in one of two battery storage systems located at the Wheeler Avenue facility, which houses the Weymouth Water Treatment Plant, according to the
Los Angeles Times
. The battery energy storage system was positioned near a solar panel field on the northeast side of the facility.
Fire crews arrived to find flames in a battery storage unit, and the situation quickly escalated. By Tuesday evening, firefighters determined that an adjacent second battery storage system had also suffered damage, with battery packs entering thermal runaway—a self-sustaining chemical reaction triggered by excessive heat that can spread rapidly to neighboring batteries.
Related:
Fail-Safe BESS Technology Prevents Thermal Runaway at Single-Cell Level
One civilian was injured at the outset and transported to a hospital,
CBS Los Angeles reported
. Grace Miller Elementary School, located less than half a mile from the facility, remained closed Wednesday as a precautionary measure.
The cause of the fire remains unknown and is under investigation.
The challenge of lithium-ion battery fires
La Verne Fire Chief Brandon Coatney reiterated the unique difficulties these fires present. Once thermal runaway begins, the process cannot be stopped, and batteries will burn for hours—or in cases involving multiple battery systems, for days. The fires release toxic gases including hydrogen fluoride, hydrogen chloride, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide,
the Los Angeles Times reported
. (You can find a detailed explanation of thermal runaway and its causes here: "
What Is Thermal Runaway? Here’s a Battery of Answers
"Later in the day, we were able to get that first battery storage system to a relatively stable point, to where it was not putting off any hazardous plume and the heat signature had gone down quite a bit," Coatney said at a Wednesday morning news conference.
Ernie Hernandez of the L.A. County Fire Department's hazardous materials team reported that air quality monitoring had not detected hazardous battery components in the vapor, though evacuation orders remained in place for homes immediately surrounding the facility as crews worked to cool the batteries with water.
Related:
How AI is Driving the Fastest Shift in Stationary Battery Applications in Decades
Prevention and detection technologies
The La Verne incident highlights why battery safety research has become increasingly urgent as BESS installations proliferate across the country. Several emerging technologies aim to prevent such fires or detect problems before they escalate.
Early warning systems
Metis Engineering's Cell Guard technology represents one approach to early detection. The system
monitors volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that batteries emit before failure
, providing crucial minutes to prevent thermal runaway from developing. This early detection capability could prove vital in facilities like the one in La Verne, where adjacent battery systems can be affected by a single unit's failure.
Thermal runaway induced in a lithium-ion battery cell for testing purposes by Metis Engineering. Credit: Metis Engineering
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has developed an
AI-based acoustic detection system
that identifies battery failures by sound. In collaboration with Xi'an University of Science and Technology, NIST recorded sounds from 38 battery explosions to train the AI system, enabling it to recognize the acoustic signatures of impending failure.
Thermal management solutions
Related:
NeoVolta, SK On Announce One of Largest Domestic Battery Deals Since OBBBA Passage
Startup CARRAR has developed
immersion cooling technology using phase-change materials
that can prevent thermal runaway from spreading between battery cells. This approach addresses the exact scenario that unfolded in La Verne, where thermal runaway in one storage system threatened adjacent units.
A CARRAR battery in the lab. Credit: CARRAR
Viridi's anti-propagation technology takes a different approach, preventing thermal runaway from spreading beyond a single battery cell through
modular design and advanced containment systems
. Their fail-safe BESS technology aims to stop cascading failures at the cell level.
Material science advances
Research into modified electrodes and bio-inspired materials offers another prevention avenue. Thermal insulation remains the most widely used mitigation strategy, but newer materials can better withstand or mitigate temperature increases that trigger thermal runaway.
Industry response
The battery industry has increasingly focused on safety as BESS installations expand. Prevention strategies include product regulation, safety standards, and advanced monitoring systems that track pressure, temperature, and gas emissions.
Infrared cameras and multi-sensor warning systems provide additional layers of protection, though the La Verne incident demonstrates that even with modern safety measures, battery fires remain a significant challenge for first responders and facility operators.
Looking ahead
As battery energy storage systems become essential for grid stability and renewable energy integration, incidents like the La Verne fire underscore the critical importance of continued investment in safety technology. The combination of early detection systems, advanced thermal management, improved materials, and comprehensive monitoring represents the industry's best path forward.
As of Wednesday, La Verne residents await the all-clear as firefighters continue cooling operations, a reminder that while battery technology powers our clean energy future, managing its risks remains an evolving challenge requiring constant vigilance and innovation.

title: What Is Black Mass in Lithium-Ion Batteries?
content:
Battery Recycling
Lithium-Ion Batteries
Batteries
Materials
Understanding black mass extracted from spent lithium-ion batteries is key to sustainable energy, supply chain resilience, and circular economies.
September 23, 2026
3 Min Read
Reclaimed materials from lithium-ion batteries.
John Keeble /Getty Images News
As the world transitions to cleaner energy sources, demand for lithium-ion batteries has surged, especially for electric vehicles (EVs), battery energy storage systems (BESS), and consumer electronics. However, this surge has also raised concerns about battery supply chain resilience, critical mineral allocations, and environmental impact. Black mass, a key component of battery recycling, offers a promising solution to these challenges. But what exactly is black mass, and why is it so important?
Understanding black mass
Black mass is a dark, powdery substance extracted from spent lithium-ion batteries during recycling. It is essentially a concentrated mixture of valuable metals and materials that are integral to manufacturing lithium-ion batteries. The name "black mass" comes from its dark, granular appearance, resulting from shredding and processing used batteries.
lithium-ion batteries
reach the end of their life cycle, they are disassembled, and their components are separated. The black mass is derived from the cathode and anode of the batteries, which contain critical minerals such as:
Related:
GM Launches Closed-Loop EV Battery Recycling Pilot Program
Manganese
Graphite
These critical minerals are essential for manufacturing new batteries, making black mass a valuable resource for battery supply chain resilience and for the circular economy.
The process of extracting black mass
Producing black mass involves several steps, starting with collecting used lithium-ion batteries. These batteries then undergo mechanical and chemical processes to recover critical minerals. The key steps include:
Battery collection and sorting: Used batteries are gathered and sorted based on their chemistry and size.
Shredding: The batteries are mechanically shredded to break them down into smaller components.
Separation: Advanced techniques, such as sieving and density separation, are used to isolate the black mass from other materials like plastics, aluminum, and copper.
Chemical processing: Hydrometallurgical or pyrometallurgical methods are employed to extract individual metals from the black mass.
GM engineers prepare an EV battery pack for testing. Courtesy of General Motors Co.
American companies leading the way in battery recycling
The US is home to several innovative companies that are at the forefront of
battery recycling
. These organizations are developing cutting-edge technologies to recover valuable materials from used lithium-ion batteries and contribute to a sustainable energy future. Key players include Redwood Materials, Cirba Solutions, American Battery Technology Company (ABTC), and more.
These companies are addressing the environmental challenges posed by battery waste and helping the US reduce its dependence on foreign sources of critical minerals, enhancing supply-chain resilience.
Related:
What Really Happens to Spent EV Batteries?
The future of battery recycling
As the demand for lithium-ion batteries continues to rise, battery recycling is poised to play a pivotal role in the global energy transition. A growing number of companies are adopting closed-loop recycling systems to extract black mass and reintegrate materials recovered from spent batteries into new battery production. For example, companies like Redwood Materials, Cirba Solutions, and GM are creating closed-loop systems.

title: AI Cuts Battery Testing Costs for Manufacturers
content:
Battery Manufacturing
EV Batteries
Automotive & Mobility
European manufacturers EAS Batteries and BMW Group each deploy machine learning models to predict cell performance, cutting development cycles from years to months.
September 23, 2026
6 Min Read
University of Zagreb and BMW researchers implement AI models for optimizing cell production.
BMW Group
At a Glance
EAS Batteries aims to boost cell service life by 10% and production yield by 15% through AI models
BMW Group cut material and time usage by over 50% in individual battery production testing processes
Traditional battery testing takes years as engineers must physically test every parameter set fully
Behind every new EV battery is a manufacturer that has spent years developing and refining its production process. The most costly step in that development cycle is testing. To validate real-world performance, battery engineers need to build new cells with real material and test them thoroughly over weeks or months. Engineers also need to hold onto valuable material and equipment throughout the testing process, which prevents them from developing other cell designs at the same time.
In the past, battery manufacturers could cover these high testing costs with higher prices. However, as
average battery prices have steadily fallen in recent years
, manufacturers have had to lower prices to remain competitive. All battery producers have therefore lost margins, some more than others. To recoup losses, companies are looking for ways to reduce testing costs because they have an outsized impact on overall product development costs.
Related:
$16 Million Prize to Boost US Critical Minerals Workforce
A growing number of battery producers see AI as a promising solution. These companies envision engineers using AI models trained on production and test data to predict how a process change will affect the finished cell before they run a test. With AI tools, engineers could validate the same cell technology with fewer tests and less time than traditional testing.
In recent months,
Battery Technology
has covered AI use in battery production by startups including
QuantumScape
SandboxAQ
as well as major research organizations such as
Honda R&D
. In this piece, we'll explain how AI can help battery engineers and two European manufacturers,
BMW Group
EAS Batteries
, that are leading their own AI projects.
AI’s appeal for battery manufacturers
Before releasing a new battery to market, manufacturers must perfect their production process to create cells with the desired performance consistently. Ordinarily, battery engineers rely on trial and error to find the optimal production settings. They would tweak a setting, like electrode coating, build a real cell, and physically test it. By testing many settings, engineers can gradually identify which production process yields the best cells.
Unfortunately, this testing approach is very costly. Trial-and-error is inherently slower than more efficient methods like predictions or simulations. The production line has many settings, and each setting affects the others, so engineers must test every parameter combination separately. Each test can also involve charging and discharging a cell hundreds of times over months so engineers can determine when the cell degrades. Because of these factors, battery testing often takes years to complete.
Related:
Tapping Battery Compound Production Potential
Close test chamber for eight pouch cells. Credit: Inficon.
To shorten the testing process, many battery engineers use
design of experiments (DOE)
, which is a statistical method that identifies ideal combinations for testing. DOE helps engineers reduce the number of tests, but they still spend time and resources building and physically evaluating each remaining test combination.
AI is a much more promising solution. Manufacturers already have the data AI models need, including coating measurements, defect images, and charging curves for every cell produced. With this data, engineers can train a model and ask it to find and evaluate production setting combinations they have never considered before.
Today’s AI models are more than capable for this application, as evidenced by a
2019 study
in which researchers used machine learning to predict LFP cell cycle life. The only remaining barrier is for battery producers to implement AI in real production environments.
Building a virtual cell at EAS Batteries
In July, a German consortium, led by EAS Batteries,
launched
a project to apply AI to battery production. Called KiBa-Pro, the project aims to combine the efforts of multiple partners to digitalize LFP cell production through June 2029. It’s received 2.4 million euros from the German Federal Ministry for Research, Technology and Space, and includes universities like Karlsruhe Institute of Technologie, and companies like Omron Europe.
Related:
Trump's Orders Secure Bulk Power System, Critical Minerals
KiBa-Pro targets LFP because
the chemistry is used in more than half of EV batteries and over 90% of energy storage systems
. The project aims to build a virtual LFP cell that battery manufacturers can use to simulate how different production settings affect the finished cell's properties. For example, an engineer can input coating thickness, porosity, throughput, and temperature data into the virtual cell and receive the expected service life and energy capacity.
Diagram of how EAS Batteries will coordinate its partners in KiBa-Pro development. Credit: EAS Batteries.
According to EAS, KiBa-Pro will help manufacturers increase cell service life by at least 10% and production yield by at least 15%. If the project meets those targets, battery producers can significantly reduce wasted material from testing and speed up new cell development.
These benefits are far from a guarantee because the project just started. EAS and its consortium plan to spend the rest of the first year capturing the production process digitally and running reference batches for AI training. Next, they plan to build out the model and validate it in industrial production over two years.
Predicting cell performance at BMW Group
In 2024, BMW Group and the University of Zagreb in Croatia
launched a joint project called Insight to apply AI across battery cell production
. The partners work at BMW's Battery Cell Competence Center (BCCC) in Munich, where BMW Group develops cell chemistry and production processes. Since the project started, researchers at BCCC have been training an AI system on past test data and live production data to predict process parameters and cell performance.
With predictions from the AI systems, engineers can quickly decide whether to shorten a test series or drop it. BMW
that teams using these predictions have cut material and time usage in individual process steps by more than 50%.
With the Insight joint research project, BMW Group and the University of Zagreb develop and implement practical AI models to optimize battery cell production. Credit: BMW Group.
In addition to improving testing, BMW claims that the Insight project can also speed up the final approval step in the battery production process. Typically, after a cell is charged for the first time at the end of production, it needs to be stored at a set temperature for a period of time to allow defects to appear. The company says that because its AI systems can fully analyze the cells for defects in advance, it can eliminate the final storage step.
While the Insight project has yielded promising results, BMW has proven the benefits only in a prototype environment. As the company readies the AI systems for a live production environment, BMW says it will transfer testing to a near-production facility in Parsdorf, Germany.
The Promise of future savings
To date, BMW and its Insight project have reported positive prototype results and are working to scale them into a live production environment. Meanwhile, the EAS-led KiBa-Pro project is currently capturing production data and plans to deliver real results by 2029.
Despite their promise, neither project has shown benefits on a running production line. In addition, neither project was designed to work across multiple factories simultaneously. Because each model is trained on one factory’s equipment and materials, what works at one site may not necessarily work at another. Only when an AI system works universally for any battery producer can companies recover lost margin from falling battery prices and release better batteries sooner.

title: Gartner Predicts Low Uptake on AI Supply Chain Planning
content:
Gartner Predicts Low Uptake on AI Supply Chain Planning
Prioritise Us
on Google
Gartner finds that organisations are unlikely to use AI for supply chain planning decisions (Credit: Getty Images)
According to Gartner, as few as 5% organisations will use AI for supply chain planning decisions by 2030, suggesting a desire for human oversight
Though news of AI adoption has been widespread across the supply chain, with it slowly becoming integrated through every step of the process, Gartner predicts there is still a reluctance to overly rely on the technology.
Large investments into automation and AI are being made, but teams are unwilling to give up their human oversight.
Supply chain technology
Automation and AI have become critical tools for many supply chain leaders in recent years, particularly as the market has become so complex. The tools are used to pull data, create analyses and make operations more efficient.
However, recent innovations have taken this one step further, letting the
AI agent
conduct the final decision-making. Previously, the agents would develop solutions or suggestions, but the human would have the final say.
In a bid to make supply chain processes more autonomous, the agents can now act entirely on their own.
Though some organisations are eager to utilise the most modern technology and prioritise automation, Gartner’s research demonstrates that leaders still want to be involved in the process.
Supply chains around the world are investing heavily in automation and AI, but Gartner suggests the
progression to autonomous planning
will be slow. This is because leaders still want to maintain control and are not wholly confident in data and technology readiness.
“Spending millions on supply chain planning automation can expand technical capabilities, but investment alone does not create AI readiness,” explains Buse Aras, Director Analyst in Gartner's Supply Chain practice.
“Leaders must establish the necessary decision, talent and technology foundations before scaling AI-enabled planning. Otherwise, they risk funding technology that does not improve the planning decisions that matter most.”
Gartner’s research
Only 5% of organisations will make 10% of planning decisions with AI by 2030
83% of organisations have spent at least US$3m on automating supply chain planning
51% of organisations have spent between US$3m and US$10m on automation and AI in supply chain planning
Evolution of planning with AI. Credit: Gartner
Costs and benefits
The pace of technological adoption is not a one-size-fits all deal. Instead, it is determined by the type, complexity and risk of each planning decision. There is greater opportunity for automation in routine operational decisions, whereas human judgement is still required for
more strategic
decisions.
Order prioritisation and replenishment can be conducted by automation, but planning to do with policy and network design cannot be – or leaders are more reluctant to try.
integrating AI into the decision-making
process, leaders need to ensure their data quality is accurate and they have strong technology architecture. Otherwise, the automation tools may cost organisations significant amounts, without demonstrating any benefits.
A Gartner survey, conducted in November-December 2025, found that 51% of organisations spent between US$3m and US$10m on the automation of their supply chain planning.
With this, the human role of the supply chain planner is changing – it is less about collecting data and more about orchestrating the developments.
Spending millions on supply chain planning automation can expand technical capabilities, but investment alone does not create AI readiness.
Buse Aras, Director Analyst in Gartner's Supply Chain practice
Supply chain leaders need to categorise their tasks. Credit: Getty
Planning strategy
As many leaders are facing issues with finding value from supply chain automation and large-scale investments, leaders need to be more strategic with how
they are integrating technology
Part of this requires greater classification – is the priority decision a strategic, tactical or operational one? By deciding on that, leaders can then determine whether the task can be completed by automation, or if it is one which will find value from human judgement.
Each task also has different requirements, so planning leaders should assess what is needed to execute the decision at its most effective level. AI and automation can be used for flexibility, which should be used to the full advantage in order to work alongside existing systems.
Success should not be measured by how much technology has been deployed, but whether it is doing what it is supposed to. If it is not reducing manual workloads or improving effectiveness then a different approach is needed.
Planning is specific, meaning each goal needs to be approached with a different tactic. Once supply chain leaders recognise this, technology can be used more effectively, but it can also work in harmony with a human workforce.

title: The Impact of the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Merger
content:
The Impact of the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Merger
Prioritise Us
on Google
Momentum is increasing for the Norfolk Southern - Union Pacific merger. Credit: Union Pacific Corporation
Union Pacific CEO, Jim Vena, explains that momentum is increasing for the merger with Norfolk Southern, with ongoing opportunities intermodal expansion
In 2025, it was announced that Union Pacific Corporation and Norfolk Southern Corporation were
proposing a merger
The transaction was valued at US$85m and would create the largest freight network in North America.
More than a year later, the merger is still in discussion, but leaders feel confident that the proposition is growing momentum and will have strong results for
logistics operations
A merger in the making
Freight railroads have undergone significant changes in the past several decades. In the 1980s, the US had more than 30 major freight railroads in operations. By July 2025, this had reduced to six, with 90% of all rail freight being accounted for by four companies.
At this time, Union Pacific announced its proposal to acquire Norfolk Southern, in a transaction of approximately US$85bn. This merger is anticipated to have a valuation of more than US$250bn and will operate under the Union Pacific name.
If the merger is approved, the company will operate more than 52,000 miles of track, making up the largest network in North America, with coast-to-coast connectivity.
Though concerns about the reduction in Class 1 railroads are high,
Jim Vena
, CEO of Union Pacific, and Mark George, President and CEO of Norfolk Southern, are working to drive this merger forward.
“The momentum behind this transaction continues to build, and we are ready to keep moving forward,” explains Jim Vena, Union Pacific CEO.
“As we said at the beginning: this merger is all about increasing growth and competition. It's good for our employees, customers and America.”
Jim Vena, CEO of Union Pacific
Key numbers
The transaction was valued at approximately US$85bn
The value of the merger is estimated in excess of US$250bn
More than 52,000 miles of track would be covered
Seven new premium intermodal lanes would be created
10,000 existing interline lanes would be converted to single-line services
43 states would be connected
Approximately 100 ports in North America would be served with the merger
Updates to the application
After more than a year of pushing for this merger, the two companies have now shared two milestones within the progress. The Surface Transportation Board (STB) has rejected opponents’ request to dismiss the merger application. As a result, the board can continue to review the merger analysis, in order to discuss whether the merger will be approved.
According to Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, the merger will result in a seamless, coast-to-coast railroad. Through this, there will be greater efficiency and affordability within
. They also argue that, by combining the railroads, more than two million truckloads will be removed from the highway.
Previously, there were concerns from unions about the merger, but a secondary milestone that has been announced is that of support from the the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation’s Railroad Mechanical Department (SMART-MD). It has entered a jobs-for-life agreement with the railroads, working to protect and preserve opportunities.
“The STB’s decision marks another important step in bringing Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern together, and we welcome the opportunity to continue sharing the many benefits of this transformative transaction,” says Norfolk Southern President and CEO Mark George.
“The combination will create new opportunities for customers across merchandise, bulk and intermodal markets through a more connected, efficient rail network. As the process moves forward, we are glad to add SMART-MD to a growing list of labor supporters, helping to ensure that we will grow together while
protecting opportunities
for railroaders.”
Mark George, President and Chief Executive Officer at Norfolk Southern
Pros of the merger
The application states that every employee with a union job when the merger is approved will have one for life, protecting security and calming previous concerns.
With regards to external benefits of the merger, the combined resources will mean that customers will have access to a more cost effective and faster cross-country railroad. As the lines will be more interconnected, less interchanges are needed, which are time-consuming and produce a certain level of risk.
With this, merchandise and bulk traffic will undergo less handoffs, resulting in lower inventory and
asset costs
. Having greater control and less handover periods, means security for the products and greater insight into where issues might occur.
The proposed merger is subject to STB review and approval, with expectations of transaction completion by the end of 2027.
The merger, as UNion Pacific and Norfolk Southern argue, will result in more streamlined logistics services for supply chains around North America, with lower costs for organisations and greater delivery speed.
In the modern era of high demand and competitive logistics operations, this merger will increase competition quality and will position the combined railroad as a leader in transportation.
It's good for our employees, customers and America.
Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena
Key companies
Union Pacific
CEO: Jim Vena
HQ: Nebraska, US
Class 1 freight railroad operator and merger lead based in Omaha, Nebraska, operating 32,400 route miles across 23 western US states. Valued at approximately US$85bn transaction to acquire Norfolk Southern. Under CEO Jim Vena's leadership, aims to create coast-to-coast network exceeding 52,000 miles serving 43 states and 100 North American ports, converting 10,000 interline lanes to single-line service for enhanced supply chain efficiency.
Norfolk Southern
CEO: Mark George
HQ: Georgia, US
Class 1 railroad headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, operating 19,300 route miles across 22 eastern states and District of Columbia. President and CEO Mark George leads merger negotiations creating estimated US$250bn combined entity. Network specializes in intermodal, merchandise and bulk freight serving automotive, agriculture, chemicals, metals and consumer goods sectors. Merger promises seamless coast-to-coast connectivity eliminating time-consuming interchange delays.
Surface Transportation Board (STB)
Chairman: Patrick Fuchs
HQ: Washington, US
Independent federal regulatory agency overseeing economic regulation of freight rail transportation in the United States. Reviews and approves major railroad mergers, ensuring competitive markets and public interest protection. Rejected opponents' dismissal requests in 2026, allowing continued merger analysis. Holds authority over transaction completion, with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern anticipating final approval and deal closure by end of 2027.
SMART Transportation Division (SMART-MD)
General President: Michael Coleman
HQ: Ohio, US
International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation's Railroad Mechanical Department representing skilled railroad workers across North America. Entered jobs-for-life agreement with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern, guaranteeing employment security for every unionized employee at merger approval. Support represents critical milestone addressing labor concerns and ensuring workforce protection throughout 52,000-mile integrated network expansion and operational transformation

content:
Why Coca-Cola is Investing $10bn in US Supply Chain
Prioritise Us
on Google
The Coca-Cola Company has released an independent study measuring the 2025 economic contribution of its US system, spanning the company's own operations and its network of 61 bottling partners. Credit: Getty Images
John Murphy, President and CFO of The Coca-Cola Company, says it is reinforcing the resilience of its US supply chain through a US$10bn investment
The Coca-Cola Company has released an independent study measuring the 2025 economic contribution of its
US system
, spanning the company's own operations and its network of 61 bottling partners.
company’s supply chain
contributes US$85bn to the US gross domestic product and supports nearly one million jobs across the country.
To reinforce its presence in the US, the company is planning US$10bn in US infrastructure investments from 2026 through 2030.
John Murphy, President and Chief Financial Officer of The Coca-Cola Company, says: “Through a strong production network, local jobs, supplier partnerships and community investments, we are building on more than a century of impact while reinforcing the resilience of our system and communities across America.”
Coca-Cola in the US
The Coca-Cola system contributes US$85bn to US GDP annually, equivalent to roughly US$10m every hour
Nearly one million jobs across the US are supported through the system's operations and supply chain
American suppliers receive approximately US$37bn in spending from the Coca-Cola system
For every dollar generated, US$0.98 remains within the US economy
A planned US$10bn investment in US infrastructure is set to take place between 2026 and 2030
John Murphy, The Coca-Cola Company's President & Chief Financial Officer
Coca-Cola's US bottling network
Coca-Cola system
operates through independent bottling partners spanning from the first Coca-Cola bottling operation, established in 1899, to Liberty Coca-Cola Beverages, the newest US bottler, opening in 2017.
Operating across 14 states, Coca-Cola Consolidated is the system's largest bottler in the US by consumer reach.
The Coca-Cola system contributes approximately US$10m in US economic activity every hour and spends roughly US$37bn with American suppliers to source ingredients.
The company keeps US$0.98 of every dollar spent on its products within the US economy by sourcing, employing, producing and distributing locally.
Its production network includes more than 70 facilities and hundreds of distribution centres, with economic contributions exceeding US$1bn in 25 individual states.
We are building on more than a century of impact while reinforcing the resilience of our system
John Murphy, President and Chief Financial Officer of The Coca-Cola Company
Investing in localised supply
The company has also committed to a further US$10bn in US investment by 2030.
This includes new or expanded production, distribution and office facilities, with projects previously announced in several communities, such as California, Colorado, Indiana, Alabama, Michigan, Minnesota, Florida and New York.
Coca-Cola's heavily localised supply chain model lands at a moment when domestic sourcing has become a genuine strategic priority across
US manufacturing
Deloitte's 2026 Manufacturing Industry Outlook identifies reshoring and strengthening domestic supply chains as one of the sector's defining trends for the year.
The research highlighted the
One Big Beautiful Bill Act's
permanent tax incentives for new equipment and domestic R&D as key drivers behind the shift.
According to the 2026 USA Reshoring Survey, which included 118 OEMs and 131 Contract Manufacturers, around 63% original equipment manufacturers are planning US capital expenditure specifically to support reshoring or domestic expansion.
The survey found that 36% of original equipment manufacturers had reshored production or were actively engaged in reshoring this year, up from 29% in 2025.

title: BYD releases the first official images of the 'bigger' Seagull EV ahead of its debut
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 24 2026 - 8:50 am PT
revealed the second-generation Seagull inside and out in a series of sketches: a bigger, smarter version of its most affordable EV.
When is BYD launching the new Seagull EV?
The Seagull, sold as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini in markets outside China, is BYD’s entry-level electric hatch.
In China, the Seagull starts at just 69,900 yuan, or about $10,000. That’s much cheaper than any new vehicle in the US. To give you a better idea, the
most affordable new car in the US
is the 2026 Hyundai Venue, which starts at just over $20,500.
Even overseas, BYD’s electric hatch is among the most affordable EVs. In Europe, the Dolphin Surf starts at about €22,900 ($26,500).
It’s no wonder the low-cost electric hatch is among the world’s top-selling electric vehicles. According to Cleantechnica, the Seagull (including the Dolphin Surf and Mini) was the sixth best-selling EV globally through the first half of 2026, with over 27,500 units sold.
BYD is now preparing to launch the second-generation model. Zhang Zhuo, the general manager of BYD’s Ocean series sales division, offered a closer look at the new Seagull this week.
Zhou revealed several design sketches of the updated version with the caption: “Preserving the classic design while embracing new expression, the lines have been reshaped and the surface refreshed #BYD Second Generation Seagull# More surprises are coming soon!”
When translated into English, the first image reads: “Brand new layout” and “Space size expands together.”
Another reads: “Clean appearance” and “The driving posture is even more extreme.” The other sketches reveal new “Trident-shaped” front and rear lights and the second-generation Seagull’s “Dynamic new look.”
No other details were mentioned, but Zhuo revealed at the Chengdu Auto Show last month that the new model will be named the “Great Seagull” and will go on sale by the end of 2026.
The new Seagull also appeared in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) regulatory filing last month, revealing a few key specs.
The filing revealed that the Great Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s considerably bigger than the current Seagull, which is just 3,780 mm long.
It will also gain a more powerful 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor. In comparison, the current Seagull uses a 55 kW (75 hp) motor.
Zhuo released the first images of the new Seagull’s interior on Thursday. The updated interior features a new two-spoke steering wheel with just two control knobs on each side.
The infotainment screen appears slightly bigger, while the images don’t show an instrument cluster. A row of physical buttons is now found below the center A/C vents. Otherwise, the cabin has a clean, minimalist feel.
Like the current Seagull, the second-generation model will retain the wireless phone charger and two cupholders between the driver and passenger.
Zhuo said “the spacious interior, with its refined details and meticulous craftsmanship, is truly stunning.”
We will learn more soon, with its official debut just around the corner, but you can expect the updated version to feature BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.
Earlier this week,
several spy images
of the new Seagull undisguised surfaced online, revealing a roof-mounted LiDAR. As such, the new version will likely get an upgraded ADAS system with BYD’s God’s Eye B.
We also caught a sneak peek of the interior last month confirming several of the updates shown in the sketches released by Zhuo. The spy images revealed the larger infotainment screen, redesigned center console, and two-spoke steering wheel.
Will BYD release the second-gen model in overseas markets, like Europe and the UK? It hasn’t been confirmed, but the larger updated electric hatch is expected to launch overseas, likely as the second-gen Dolphin Surf.
The current Dolphin Surf starts at around €22,900 ($26,500) in Europe, so the larger variant will likely cost a bit more. It will likely still start at under €30,000 ($35,000), as a smaller, more affordable option than the Dolphin.

title: Tesla Semi launch sneak peek: several customers are being announced
content:
Tesla Semi
Fred Lambert
| Sep 24 2026 - 7:10 am PT
Credit: Zanegler
Tesla has lined up at least 11 Semi electric trucks wearing customer logos outside its new Nevada factory, a clear sign that the automaker plans to parade its fleet customers at tonight’s Semi launch event.
A drone flyover of the plant shows trucks branded for PepsiCo, US Foods, DHL, WattEV, ABF, Einride, IMC, OK Produce, and a few others parked in a neat row by the factory.
The footage comes from
Zanegler
, a YouTuber who calls himself a “Tesla Semi Advocate” and regularly flies his drone over Tesla’s Semi operations in Sparks, Nevada.
In the video, eight trucks sit side by side next to the factory, each with a different company logo on the roof fairing. Three more drive around the lot nearby, including one branded for PepsiCo and one for US Foods.
Here’s what we could make out from the footage:
US Foods
IMC (Logistics)
OK Produce
ABF (ArcBest)
At least two more logos are too blurry to identify with confidence, including one on a truck at the far end of the lot. If you can make them out, let us know in the comments.
Most of these are familiar names
A lot of these companies have already been part of the Tesla Semi story. PepsiCo took the
first Tesla Semi deliveries back in late 2022
DHL took delivery of its first Semi last December
after a long trial.
ArcBest’s ABF Freight
bought Semis in June after its pilot showed 1.55 kWh per mile
. Einride placed a
500-truck order in August
, and IMC Logistics announced a
50-truck order for California drayage
just two days ago.
US Foods, OK Produce, LTS, and WattEV are the more interesting additions. We haven’t reported on firm Semi orders from those companies, so Tesla will likely use the stage to confirm them.
Tonight’s event
Tesla is holding the event at its new Semi factory next to Gigafactory Nevada, with a livestream starting at 9 p.m. ET. It’s officially the
inauguration of the dedicated Semi plant
, which Tesla says can build 50,000 trucks a year.
The factory has been producing trucks since the
first Semi rolled off the high-volume line in April
. Tesla offers two versions: a Standard Range at 325 miles and a Long Range at 500 miles, both with an 800 kW three-motor powertrain.
And the order book is filling up. Tesla was named primary supplier this week for
ZET SCALE’s 2,500-truck order
, backed by Microsoft and PepsiCo, though Kenworth, Volvo, and RIDE are also in that deal.
Electrek’s Take
Nine years after the 2017 unveiling, and six years after the truck was supposed to hit production, the Semi story has been about promises. A row of trucks branded for PepsiCo, DHL, ArcBest, and US Foods says something different: real fleets are buying these things, and some of them are coming back for more.
But let’s keep it in perspective. Analysts expect Tesla to deliver somewhere between 5,000 and 15,000 Semis this year, far below the plant’s 50,000-unit capacity. We think 5,000 would be a great win, and it will likely be below that.
Tonight, we want to hear pricing and current production capacity. How many trucks have been delivered, how fast is the line ramping, and how many of these customers have committed to hundreds rather than a handful? If Tesla answers that, this event is more than a stock pump.
Fleets electrifying their trucks are learning the same lesson homeowners have: charging is cheapest when you control where your electricity comes from. title: Waymo says it has stopped 841 injuries in 271 million autonomous miles
content:
Robotaxi
Jameson Dow
| Sep 24 2026 - 6:00 am PT
Photo: Waymo
Waymo has released new crash data which claims not only an 82% reduction in crashes, but for the first time says the number of injuries that have been avoided by its robotaxi operation.
We’ve seen various Waymo crash data before, with Waymo claiming
crash reductions
That’s all well and good when the company says it, but we’ve also seen independent data confirming similar (though lower)
crash reduction numbers
. So it does seem like Waymo has an advantage over human drivers, at least in the limited areas it operates in.
The problem is, crashes are relatively rare, and crashes that cause injury even moreso. So even though Waymo’s millions of miles driven seems like a lot, human drivers drive 3
trillion
miles per year in the US. So there’s still quite a gap in the data.
Nevertheless, Waymo has enough miles that it’s ready to start quoting how many injuries it has prevented, and the number is pretty high.
Its newest crash data states that it had operated a total of 271 million driverless miles through June of this year, which is 50 million more miles added in the 3 months since its end-of-March update.
Over those miles, Waymo says there was an 82% reduction in crashes that caused injury, and a 95% reduction in crashes that cause “serious injury or worse.”
It also said that the number were even better for more vulnerable road users. Waymo says that there were 86% fewer cyclist crashes causing injury and 93% fewer pedestrian crashes causing injury.
Waymo also released some interesting video showing avoided crashes. Here are a few of them:
All told, summing up the numbers across its number of miles operated, Waymo says that 841 crashes that would have caused injury were avoided. 175 of those crashes would have involved pedestrians, cyclists or motorcyclists, and 55 of them would have caused serious injuries or worse.
These numbers are important right now, especially as fatal crashes for pedestrians and cyclists reach all time highs due to
ballooning vehicle sizes
, distracted drivers, and an intentional effort by US Transportation Secretary/former reality TV contestant Sean Duffy to
kill everyone who isn’t in a car
(yes, really).

title: U.S. solar system pricing rises for utility, C&I projects as residential costs decline - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Declining module costs are offset by elevated structural materials tariffs and surging domestic freight rates, leaving residential solar as the sole segment to see price reductions in Q2 2026.
Ryan Kennedy
24 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Commercial & industrial
Residential
Utility-scale
U.S. solar system prices increased across utility and commercial segments in the second quarter of 2026, driven by persistent structural materials tariffs and rising domestic transportation expenses, according to the latest pricing analysis from Wood Mackenzie and the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA).
Residential solar stood as the single exception to the upward pricing trend, with turnkey residential system costs dropping 1.4% year-over-year to average $3.36 per watt in Q2. Commercial solar system pricing experienced the steepest inflation, rising 5.6% year-over-year to $1.77 per watt. In the utility-scale segment, fixed-tilt system prices rose 0.9% year-over-year to $0.95 per watt, while single-axis tracking systems increased 2.0% over the same period to reach $1.06 per watt.
The top-line pricing trends reflect a widening divergence between equipment hardware costs and site-level installation logistics. While module hardware prices declined across the board, those savings were largely absorbed by rising structural, electrical, and transport expenditures.
In the distributed generation market, module prices dropped by an average of 16% year-over-year to hit $0.37 per watt in Q2. The sharp reduction followed the invalidation of International Emergency Economic Powers Act tariffs earlier in 2026, which eased trade pressure on imported solar components.
Conversely, utility-scale module price declines were far more muted. Utility module costs fell just 2% year-over-year, averaging $0.33 per watt in Q2. The muted decline stems from a widespread operational shift toward domestic procurement, as developers pay a notable premium for U.S.-manufactured modules to secure federal domestic content adders and insulate project pipelines from trade enforcement risks.
Cost reductions on modules were countered by a 15% average increase in logistics and freight expenses across all market segments. Logistics inflation has been driven primarily by higher oil and gas prices, which have jumped roughly 50% year-over-year since the start of the Middle East conflict.
Additionally, Section 232 tariffs on raw aluminum, steel, and copper continue to elevate structural and electrical balance of plant costs, affecting both imported and domestic equipment. The import duties affect both foreign supply chains and domestic equipment manufacturers relying on imported raw metals, keeping racking, tracker, and wiring costs high for developers across all scales.
Wood Mackenzie calculates its national average solar system pricing using a bottom-up modeling framework. The methodology captures overnight contracting prices incurred during the year in which the project is being contracted without factoring in procurement or construction lags. This is accomplished by combining tracked wholesale pricing of major solar components and supply chain data models with direct industry interviews.

title: Ventilator exhaust air, evaporative cooling boost residential heat pump efficiency - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
South Korean researchers have developed a residential air-source heat pump concept that combines energy recovery ventilator exhaust air with direct evaporative cooling. The system improved COP by 7.3% to 15.2% under hot and humid conditions and could be suitable for retrofitting existing heat pumps.
Lior Kahana
24 Sep 2026
Research & Development
Heat pumps
Residential
Illustration of the proposed system
A South Korean research team has proposed a residential air-source heat pump (ASHP) system that combines exhaust air from an energy recovery ventilator (ERV) with direct evaporative cooling. Tests showed the approach could reduce the heat pump’s outdoor-unit inlet air temperature by up to 6.4 C and improve its coefficient of performance (COP) by 7.3% to 15.2% under hot and humid conditions.
“In this study, a system is proposed that improves direct evaporative cooler (DEC) performance by utilizing exhaust air from an ERV, thereby enhancing the heat rejection performance of air-source heat pump (ASHP) condensers,” the researchers said. “The objective of this study is to determine how the reduction in the outdoor unit (ODU) inlet air temperature obtained by mixing the exhaust air with the outdoor air affects the refrigeration cycle and the system performance.”
The experimental setup featured a 3 kW ASHP using R410A refrigerant, with a direct evaporative cooler installed in front of its outdoor unit. The cooler consisted of a 150 mm-thick wetted pad, four spray nozzles, a water sump, and a 21 W recirculation pump delivering 3 L/min.
In the proposed configuration, outdoor air is mixed with cooler, drier exhaust air from an ERV before passing through the wetted pad and reaching the ASHP outdoor unit. The researchers said this arrangement lowers both the dry-bulb and wet-bulb temperatures of the air entering the evaporative cooler, improving its effectiveness under humid conditions.
The scientists did not physically connect an ERV during testing. Instead, they calculated the expected mixed-air conditions based on an ERV exhaust airflow rate of 100 m³/h and reproduced them in a controlled chamber. Tests were conducted at outdoor temperatures ranging from 30 C to 33 C and relative humidity levels of 60% to 70%. The indoor chamber was maintained at 24 C and 50% relative humidity, with a 4 kW electric heater providing the thermal load.
“The ERV exhaust air lowered both the dry-bulb and the wet-bulb temperature of the air entering the DEC, contributing to the cooling through a sensible and a latent effect of comparable magnitude,” the researchers said.
The resulting reduction in outdoor-unit inlet temperature lowered the heat pump’s condensing temperature and compressor work. At 32 C and a humidity ratio of 19 g/kg, the condensing temperature fell by 6.8 K and the compression ratio by 7.6% compared with the conventional configuration. Compressor work decreased by 13.8%, while the heat rejection rate fell by 2.8%.
The researchers assessed the system’s overall efficiency using a COP correlation model across the tested temperature and humidity range. They also said the proposed configuration could be suitable for retrofits, as it would only require the addition of a direct evaporative cooler to an existing heat pump and a connection to the exhaust duct of an installed ventilation system.
“The proposed system is feasible for retrofitting because it can be implemented by installing a DEC unit on an existing heat pump and utilizing the exhaust duct of the installed ventilation system without requiring facility replacement,” they said.
The system was presented in the study “
Integrating ventilator exhaust air and evaporative cooling for improving energy performance of residential air-source heat pumps
,” published in the
Journal of Building Engineering
. The research team included scientists from South Korea’s
Hanyang University
Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology

title: Brazil power producers call for BESS framework and curtailment rules - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Brazil’s independent power producers are calling for a regulatory framework for battery energy storage systems (BESS) and the country’s first storage auction, alongside clearer rules for renewable energy curtailment.
Alessandra Neris
24 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Utility-scale
Brazil’s independent power producers are calling for a regulatory framework for BESS and clearer rules for renewable energy curtailment as part of an agenda for the country’s 2027-2030 government cycle.
The Brazilian Association of Independent Electricity Producers (APINE) presented six priorities to presidential candidates, including technical criteria for managing generation restrictions, transmission expansion and measures to improve investment predictability in the power sector.
APINE wants transparent rules covering curtailment caused by both transmission constraints and periods of excess electricity supply.
In an article published by the association in September, APINE President Rui Altieri cited data from Brazil’s National Electric System Operator (ONS) showing that average restrictions on wind and solar generation reached 3,629 MW between January and July 2026, equivalent to 19.3% of the potential generation of affected plants. The figure was 16.8% over the same period in 2025.
APINE linked the increase in curtailment to the need to align power system infrastructure with the expansion of renewable generation.
The association is also calling for modernized transmission expansion planning, additional grid capacity and faster environmental licensing for strategic transmission projects.
It wants power prices and tariffs to better reflect hourly and locational system conditions, while also seeking greater regulatory and legal certainty for existing contracts and new investments.
APINE is proposing a regulatory framework covering both large-scale battery energy storage systems and reversible hydropower plants.
The association also supports Brazil’s first energy storage auction, with the costs of contracted storage services allocated among the market participants that benefit from them.
APINE said a defined contracting and cost-allocation structure will become increasingly important as the power system requires more flexibility to accommodate variable renewable generation.
The agenda also calls for a strategy to coordinate the growth of data centers, electric vehicles and green hydrogen projects with power system planning.
APINE said these new loads could increase electricity consumption in regions and periods with greater availability of generation if their development is incorporated into system expansion planning.

title: Websol secures land for 4 GW solar cell and module factory in India - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Websol Energy System has secured 21.9 hectares of land in West Bengal for a new solar manufacturing facility. The plant will have 4 GW each of solar cell and module production capacity, developed in two 2 GW phases.
Uma Gupta
24 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Websol Energy System Ltd
has secured 21.9 hectares of land at Falta Industrial Park in the Indian state of West Bengal for a planned solar manufacturing facility.
The factory will have 4 GW of annual solar cell production capacity and 4 GW of module capacity. Websol plans to develop the project in two phases of 2 GW each.
The land allotment forms part of Websol’s plans to expand its manufacturing operations in West Bengal, where it already operates a solar cell and module factory in the Falta Special Economic Zone (SEZ).
Websol said its existing presence in the state provides access to skilled workers, established supplier relationships and familiarity with the local manufacturing ecosystem, which it expects will support the development of the new facility.
The project will expand Websol’s manufacturing footprint in eastern India.
“When Websol entered solar manufacturing in the mid-1990s, the industry in India was still at a very early stage. Today, solar is becoming an increasingly important part of the country’s energy infrastructure, and the need for strong domestic manufacturing has never been clearer,” said Sohan Lal Agarwal, chairman and managing director of Websol Energy System.
“For us, this land allotment represents the next phase of a journey that began more than three decades ago in West Bengal,” Agarwal added. “It allows us to build at a significantly larger scale while remaining close to an ecosystem, workforce and operating base we know well. As India expands its solar capacity, we believe manufacturing must grow alongside it, across regions and closer to demand.”
Sanjana Khaitan, executive director of Websol Energy System, said the company will now focus on moving the project from land allotment to construction, commissioning and production.
Founded in 1990, Websol manufactures solar cells and modules. It primarily supplies cells to the Indian market, including module manufacturers seeking to comply with domestic content requirement (DCR) rules. The company sells its modules in India and overseas.
Websol’s existing Falta SEZ facility has 1.2 GW of annual solar cell production capacity and 550 MW of module capacity. Its production lines can process wafers up to 210 mm.
Websol is among the manufacturers included on India’s Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for solar cells.

title: Second-life PV modules turned into solar balconies in Germany - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
A reuse project in Kassel, Germany, has repurposed 300 used solar modules to create 150 balcony PV systems, with tiered pricing aimed at improving affordability. The 13-year-old panels were inspected and refurbished, with local organizations providing technical, logistical and financial support.
Pilar Sánchez Molina
24 Sep 2026
Applications & Installations
Residential
A photovoltaic reuse initiative in Kassel, Germany, has repurposed 300 used solar modules to create 150 balcony PV systems.
The panels, which had operated for 13 years on the roof of an industrial building, were inspected, refurbished and distributed to participants in an upcycling project organized by ClimateHub Kassel and solar collective SoLocal Energy.
The project began with inspections of the 300 recovered modules. Twelve panels showed minor defects and were discarded, while the remaining modules were cleaned and fitted with new connectors for use in balcony PV systems. The recovered modules represent around 6 metric tons of material that would otherwise have entered recycling streams, where only certain material fractions can be recovered.
The organizers introduced a tiered pricing model to make the systems accessible to households with different budgets. Complete packages include modules, an inverter, mounting equipment, cabling and accessories, as well as electrical connection, system registration and monitoring setup.
A system comprising two 325 W CSW Excellent modules, for a total capacity of 650 W, costs €825 ($937) under the subsidized tariff, €1,000 at the standard rate and €1,175 under the solidarity tariff. A single-module system costs €650, €775 and €900, respectively. A four-module configuration using CSW Diamond panels has a combined capacity of 1.78 kW and costs €2,025 under the highest pricing tier specified by the organizers.
Participants can also collect the equipment and install the systems themselves. Two-module systems are supplied with a Hoymiles HMS-800W-2T microinverter. Three- and four-module systems use either two SUN-M80 units or one Hoymiles HMS-1600-4WB inverter, with dynamic power control limiting total output to 800 W.
An optional storage package, comprising a Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro 2 battery and an energy meter, costs an additional €600 to €700, depending on the pricing tier. Professional-grade modules are also available for €30 more per panel than the Diamond modules.
Several local organizations provided logistical and technical support. Bauteilbörse handled 13 pallets of modules, while BürgerSolarBeratung and energy cooperative Bürgerenergiegenossenschaft Kassel & Söhre provided technical assistance. Cargo bikes were made available to help participants transport the modules.
German nonprofit organization Deutsche Gesellschaft für Sonnenenergie (DGS) also made a donation to reduce the cost of inverters and mounting equipment for some low-income households.

title: Daikin unveils air-to-air heat pumps for highly insulated homes - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
The Japanese manufacturer has introduced a new generation of its Ururu Sarara X reversible air conditioners, featuring heating capacities from 2.2 kW to 8.0 kW and a new compressor designed to improve efficiency under low-load operation.
Emiliano Bellini
24 Sep 2026
Technology & Products
Heat pumps
Residential
The Ururu Sarara X heat pump
Japanese heating system manufacturer
has unveiled a new series of residential air-to-air heat pumps that it says are particularly suitable for highly insulated, airtight homes, where heating and cooling loads can remain low for extended periods once the desired indoor temperature has been reached.
The systems use R32 as the refrigerant, which has a global warming potential (GWP) of 675, and rely on a “small-capacity, high-efficiency compressor” that can reportedly maintain efficient operation under low-load conditions, reducing the energy losses associated with frequent compressor cycling.
Initially launched in the Japanese market, the Ururu Sarara X heat pump line comprises nine models for rooms ranging from six to 26 tatami mats, a Japanese unit of floor area, corresponding to approximately 10 m² to 43 m². Five models operate with a single-phase 100 V power supply and five are available with a 200 V connection, with the 4.0 kW capacity class offered in both configurations.
The manufacturer said the new compressor is particularly suited for spaces where indoor temperatures are less affected by outdoor conditions and the units consequently spend longer periods operating at low output. According to Daikin, the technology can also contribute to meeting the energy-performance requirements of Japan’s GX-oriented and zero-energy home (ZEH) standards.
The heat pumps also feature a new outdoor-temperature-dependent “Heat Boost Control.” The function is activated when outdoor temperatures fall to 2 C or below and increases both heating capacity and airflow.
Daikin said the technology can reduce the time required to reach the set temperature by around 20% compared with its previous-generation system. In tests conducted by the manufacturer with a 4.0 kW model, the system raised the indoor temperature from 10 C to a setpoint of 22 C in approximately 14 minutes at an outdoor temperature of 2 C, compared with around 18 minutes for the previous model.
The company also said the increased airflow expands the floor area reaching temperatures of at least 22 C by approximately 1.2 times compared with the previous-generation system under its specified test conditions.
For cooling operation, Daikin has introduced a low-airflow sleep mode designed to reduce discomfort caused by drafts during the night. In the 2.2 kW to 2.8 kW models, the manufacturer said operating noise remains at 35 dB(A) or below when the function is activated.
Daikin said the Ururu Sarara X range also combines heating and cooling with humidification, dehumidification, ventilation and air purification functions, without providing further technical details.
For comparison, the previous Ururu Sarara X generation has nominal heating capacities ranging from 2.5 kW to 10.6 kW and nominal cooling capacities ranging from 2.2 kW to 9.0 kW. Depending on the model, heating output can reach up to 12.4 kW, while maximum cooling output reaches 9.1 kW.
The indoor units measure 798 mm × 295 mm × 370 mm, while the size and weight of the outdoor units vary according to capacity, from 795 mm × 713 mm × 300 mm to 850 mm × 849 mm × 320 mm.
“With the launch of the 2027 models, we aim to contribute to comfortable living and energy savings by enhancing energy efficiency and comfort in response to changes in housing performance and lifestyles,” Daikin said in a statement,

title: Spain plans to allocate 11 GW of grid capacity for renewables, storage - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Spain plans to allocate up to 11 GW of grid capacity to renewable energy and storage projects, with a dedicated tender for Guardo and Velilla attracting interest from pumped-hydro developers.
Pilar Sánchez Molina
24 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Highlights
Utility-scale
A PV plant operated by Q Energy in Spain
Spain plans to allocate up to 11 GW of grid access capacity for renewable energy and energy storage projects at transition hubs, including dedicated competitive tenders for two sites in Palencia.
The Ministry for the Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge (MITECO), through the Institute for Just Transition (ITJ), has opened two public consultations running until Oct. 8 on procedures to allocate capacity reserved at just-transition grid nodes.
The first procedure covers 15 grid nodes in transition areas across A Coruña, Almería, Asturias, Burgos, Cádiz, León, Palencia and Puertollano. The ITJ proposes allocating available capacity through a simple competitive process based on the order in which applications are received.
Projects will have to meet technical requirements, undergo applicable environmental assessments and commit to socioeconomic measures benefiting the relevant transition area.
The second procedure covers the Guardo 220 kV and Velilla 400 kV nodes in the Guardo-Velilla transition area in Palencia. The ITJ proposes a competitive tender because a market consultation identified significant interest in the two nodes, particularly from reversible hydropower projects.
The future tender will be established through a regulatory order and will assess projects against socioeconomic and environmental criteria, alongside applicable technical requirements for grid connection.
MITECO said the initial market consultation, held from April to June, was used to assess demand for the reserved capacity from renewable generation and storage projects.
The Guardo-Velilla process could provide access to grid capacity for long-duration storage projects, with reversible hydropower able to shift electricity generation between periods of lower and higher demand.
